blockTypes.paragraph: Body text: one or more full sentences that the narrator reads as content.
blockTypes.section_heading: A short heading that starts a new section of the lesson. A label, not a full sentence of content.
blockTypes.subsection_heading: A short label for one sub-point inside a section, such as a lettered or numbered sub-part ("Step 2 — Packing") or the name of one item the section goes through. Not a full sentence.
blockTypes.list_item: One item of a numbered or bulleted list.
blockTypes.list_intro: A sentence that introduces the list items directly after it, usually ending with a colon.
blockTypes.lesson_title: The title of the whole lesson, normally the very first line.
blockTypes.recap_heading: A heading that starts a summary, recap or key-takeaways section.

templates.title: Opens the video or a chapter: a title, optionally with a subtitle. Little narration beyond the title itself.
templates.statement: Makes one point that should land, or quotes someone. A single message, not a set of separate items.
templates.media: Refers to a picture, screenshot or diagram that we have as a file.
templates.sequence: Walks through ordered steps or a repeating cycle, where the order matters.
templates.comparison: Sets two or three sides against each other: alternatives (option A versus option B), or two sides of one thing (benefits versus risks, allowed versus not allowed, before versus after).
templates.rule-exception: Gives a default rule and its exceptions.
templates.tool-selection: Picks between modes of one tool depending on the situation.
templates.principle: Names one central idea and the consequences or benefits that follow from it.
templates.framework: Names the parts that together make up one whole.
templates.categories: Groups things into families or groups, each with its own members.
templates.list: Lists several things with no further structure: good points, things to do or check, or things to avoid or that are forbidden.

features: Is this scene only the title of the lesson or of a chapter, with no other content?
Does the narration quote words said or written by a named person?
Does the narration walk through steps where the order matters, or through a repeating cycle?
Does the narration set two or three sides against each other, such as option A versus option B, benefits versus risks, or what is allowed versus what is not?
Does the narration state a default rule and then the exceptions to that rule?
Does the narration explain how to choose between modes or settings of one tool?
Does the narration name one central idea and then the reasons or consequences that follow from it?
Does the narration name the parts that together make up one whole thing?
Does the narration sort things into groups that each have their own members?
Does the narration name several separate things, such as items, requirements, examples or warnings, that could be shown as a list?
brandRule: brand: when the item stands for a named product, service or company (as the narration names it), add "brand": its name exactly as the narration says it. Still give the closest icon: the icon is shown until a logo for that brand is supplied. Never tag a generic thing ("an AI model", "a chatbot") as a brand.
